## Lesson Overview
- **Topic:** Chapter 5: Work, Energy and Power
- **Grade:** Grade 11
- **Subject:** Physics
- **Duration:** 40-45 minutes
- **CBSE Unit:** Physics Chapter 5: Work, Energy and Power

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:
1. Explain the role of woman's applied force ($F$) varies linearly from 100 N at 10 m to 50 N at 20 m.
2. Explain the role of frictional force ($f$) is constant at 50 N and opposes motion.
3. Explain the role of the applied force versus displacement is a trapezoid, starting at 100 N at 10 m and decreasing to 50 N at 20 m.

I can explain the role of woman's applied force ($F$) varies linearly from 100 N at 10 m to 50 N at 20 m.
I can explain the role of frictional force ($f$) is constant at 50 N and opposes motion.
I can explain the role of the applied force versus displacement is a trapezoid, starting at 100 N at 10 m and decreasing to 50 N at 20 m.

## Prerequisites
Students should already know:
- Concepts and vocabulary introduced earlier in this unit of Physics.
- Basic terms relevant to Work, Energy and Power covered in previous lessons.

## Materials & Resources
- NCERT Textbook Grade 11 Physics
- Blackboard / Whiteboard
- Notebook for worked examples and quick notes

## Lesson Plan (Step-by-Step)

### Introduction & Hook (illustrative: 5 minutes)
- Ask: " A wooden block of mass 2 kg rests on a soft horizontal floor. When an iron cylinder of mass 5 kg is placed on top of the wooden block, the entire..." Take a few answers from students.
- Tell students today's lesson covers Work, Energy and Power.

### Direct Instruction (illustrative: 15 minutes)
- Woman's applied force ($F$) varies linearly from 100 N at 10 m to 50 N at 20 m.
- Frictional force ($f$) is constant at 50 N and opposes motion.
- The applied force versus displacement is a trapezoid, starting at 100 N at 10 m and decreasing to 50 N at 20 m.
- Friction force is a constant 50 N, acting opposite to the direction of motion.
- The work done is the area under the force-displacement graph from 0 to 20 m.
- Worked example:  A wooden block of mass 2 kg rests on a soft horizontal floor. When an iron cylinder of mass 5 kg is placed on top of the wooden block, the entire... Answer:  The force exerted by the wooden block on the iron cylinder is 15 N to the right.

### Guided Practice (illustrative: 10 minutes)
- As a class, work through one more example illustrating Woman's applied force ($F$) varies linearly from 100 N at 10 m to 50 N at 20 m..

### Student Activity (illustrative: 10 minutes)
- In pairs, students apply today's core idea (The applied force versus displacement is a trapezoid, starting at 100 N at 10 m and decreasing to 50 N at 20 m.) to a new example of their own or one provided by the teacher, and explain their reasoning in 2-3 sentences.
- 2-3 pairs share their answers; teacher confirms accurate understanding.

### Assessment & Closure (illustrative: 5 minutes)
- Quick oral questions checking the core objectives covered today.
- Summary: recap the main ideas covered in this lesson.
- Exit ticket: "In one sentence, explain the role of woman's applied force ($F$) varies linearly from 100 N at 10 m to 50 N at 20 m"

## Homework Assignment
- Practice one more example similar to today's lesson on Work, Energy and Power, showing your reasoning steps.

## Differentiation Strategies
- **For students needing additional support:** Provide a simplified worked example on Woman's applied force ($F$) varies linearly from 100 N at 10 m to 50 N at 20 m., with key terms pre-defined and one step already completed as a model.
- **For students ready for extension:** Ask them to apply the idea of The applied force versus displacement is a trapezoid, starting at 100 N at 10 m and decreasing to 50 N at 20... to a new, unfamiliar example and justify their answer in writing.
